finding.claim: publicUrl() concatenates the storage path into the URL without percent-encoding, so keys containing %, ?, or # produce URLs that resolve to a different object than the stored key (e.g. '%2e%2e' segments decoded by the origin server to '..', or '#'/'?' truncating the path). Same defect in ShardedPrefixPublicUrlGenerator.php:37.
finding.source: Object key/path supplied by the application's caller, which is attacker-influenced when uploads keep client-supplied filenames (e.g. 'a/%2e%2e/secret' or 'victim.png#x').
finding.sink: Returned public URL string (PrefixPublicUrlGenerator.php:21 / ShardedPrefixPublicUrlGenerator.php:37) handed to clients or embedded in pages.

trace.note: path normalized, but normalizer does not encode or reject %, ?, #
delegates to prefixPath with raw path
prefix . ltrim(path) — plain string concatenation, no encoding

finding.guards_checked: WhitespacePathNormalizer.php:25-29 rejects control characters only; :39-42 rejects '..' above root; neither encodes URL-reserved characters. No rawurlencode/urlencode anywhere on the URL path. Exploitability depends on the origin decoding percent-escapes and serving the storage root directly (not verifiable here: adapters are absent).

finding.claim: Fail-open visibility mapping: inverseForFile() and inverseForDirectory() return PUBLIC for any mode that is not exactly the configured filePublic/filePrivate (or directory equivalents). A private object with e.g. mode 0640 (common under umask 027) is reported as public, and cross-filesystem copies that retain visibility then write it to the destination as public.
finding.source: Permission bits of the source object on the storage backend (not attacker-chosen directly; a precondition of non-standard modes).
finding.sink: Destination writeStream with visibility='public' (world-readable object created from a formerly non-public source).

trace.note: no explicit visibility → read from source
sourceFilesystem->visibility() → adapter inverse mapping (adapter not in repo)
unknown mode falls through to PUBLIC (same at line 58 for directories)

finding.guards_checked: PortableVisibilityGuard.php:9-17 validates only inputs to forFile/forDirectory, not the inverse direction. Retain-visibility path is the default, so no opt-in needed. Whether the real adapter uses this converter could not be confirmed.

finding.claim: move()/copy() decide same-filesystem vs cross-filesystem by object identity of the FilesystemOperator. Two mount keys backed by different operator instances that share the same underlying storage location take the copy-then-delete path; when source and destination resolve to the same physical object, the copy overwrites it and the subsequent delete removes it, causing data loss.
finding.source: Mount keys and paths chosen by the caller; requires aliased mounts (configuration) and a caller that lets the same relative path be used across them.
finding.sink: Source delete after copy (protected operation: data destruction).

trace.note: destination resolved to operator B (different instance, same storage)

finding.guards_checked: Filesystem::move identical-path check (Filesystem.php:127-135) only runs inside a single operator, so it is bypassed across mounts. No path comparison across mounts exists in MountManager.
